info.name: open-terminal
info.description:
Open Terminal — the code-execution backend for this Open WebUI deployment (`ghcr.io/open-webui/open-terminal`, see ai/open-terminal/OPEN_TERMINAL.md).

**There is no host port and no LiteLLM pass-through.** Unlike every other collection in this repo, these requests do NOT go through `{{litellm}}`. `open-terminal` publishes nothing to the host and sits alone with `openwebui` on the `terminal_net` bridge, because it is a root-capable shell driven by a model — see OPEN_TERMINAL.md § Network isolation. Every production request is proxied by the Open WebUI BACKEND (`backend/open_webui/routers/terminals.py`), which adds `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, `X-User-Id`, and `X-Session-Id` server-side.

**To use this collection you must reach the container yourself.** Pick one:

1. *Preferred, nothing to undo* — run curl from inside openwebui, using this collection as the reference for paths and bodies:
   `docker exec openwebui curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPEN_TERMINAL_API_KEY" http://open-terminal:8000/openapi.json`
2. *Temporary loopback publish* — add `ports: ["127.0.0.1:8000:8000"]` to the `open-terminal` service, `make up open-terminal`, debug, then REMOVE it and recreate. Never bind 0.0.0.0: the bearer token is the only thing between the LAN and a shell.
3. *Ad-hoc tunnel* — `docker run --rm --network terminal_net -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 alpine/socat tcp-listen:8000,fork,reuseaddr tcp-connect:open-terminal:8000`.

Then set the collection variables `openTerminal` (default `http://localhost:8000`) and `openTerminalApiKey` (= `OPEN_TERMINAL_API_KEY` in .env) — every request inherits the bearer token from collection-level auth.

**Multi-user mode is on**, so `X-User-Id` decides which Linux account and `/home/<user>` a call touches. Requests that care about it send the `openTerminalUserId` variable; leave it blank to act as the default `user` account. `X-Session-Id` (`openTerminalSessionId`) scopes the remembered working directory, the process list and the PTY sessions (each owned by its X-User-Id + X-Session-Id pair).

Endpoints marked *“not in the OpenAPI schema”* carry `include_in_schema=False` upstream: they are reachable over HTTP and used by the Open WebUI UI, but they are NOT turned into function-calling tools for the model. The schema'd ones are.

Source of truth for shapes: `open_terminal/main.py` at the tag pinned in `OPEN_TERMINAL_VERSION`.

**Error bodies.** Each endpoint's `#### Schemas` section -- at the end of its first request's description, generated from `open-terminal.schemas.json` by `scripts/api_schemas.py render` -- documents the fields this stack uses of each request and response body: an open subset of the upstream API. Any other error answers FastAPI's `{"detail": "<message>"}`; a request that fails validation answers 422 `{"detail": [{"type", "loc", "msg", "input", ...}]}`, one entry per problem.

variable.description: Base URL for open-terminal. There is NO host publish by default — this value assumes you set up one of the three access routes described in the collection description (docker exec, a temporary 127.0.0.1 port, or a socat tunnel). From inside the openwebui container the address is http://open-terminal:8000.

OPEN_TERMINAL_API_KEY from .env — the same value ai/openwebui/docker-compose.openwebui.yml interpolates into TERMINAL_SERVER_CONNECTIONS. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{openTerminalApiKey}}` by the collection-level auth. Treat it as a root-capable credential: anyone holding it gets a shell on the box.

Value for the X-User-Id header. In multi-user mode (OPEN_TERMINAL_MULTI_USER=true) open-terminal maps this to a Linux account and runs the call under `sudo -u`, so it selects which /home/<user> you are operating on. In production it is the Open WebUI user id, set by the backend proxy. Leave blank to act as the default `user` account.

Value for the X-Session-Id header — the chat/session id. Scopes the remembered working directory (GET/POST /files/cwd, and relative-path resolution everywhere else) the process list from GET /execute, and the PTY sessions of /api/terminals. Entries expire after OPEN_TERMINAL_SESSION_CWD_TTL (7 days, refreshed on access). Optional.
Process id returned by POST /execute (format `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<6 hex>`). Paste it here and the status / input / kill requests under Execute pick it up.
8-char interactive PTY session id returned by POST /api/terminals. UNRELATED to openTerminalSessionId — that one is the chat id sent in a header; this one is a live pseudo-terminal handle.

item.name: Files
item.description: The file API behind Open WebUI's file-browser sidebar, previews, and chat uploads. Relative paths resolve against the session cwd when X-Session-Id is sent, otherwise against the user's home. Note the split between `/files/read` (LLM-facing: text, extracted document text, or an image; refuses other binaries) and `/files/view` (UI-facing: raw bytes of anything, optional rendered preview).

request.description:
Read a file for LLM consumption: `{"path", "total_lines", "content"}`, optionally narrowed to a line range. Three behaviours by type:

- text → JSON as above
- documents (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, ODF …) → extracted text, same JSON shape
- binary whose MIME matches OPEN_TERMINAL_BINARY_MIME_PREFIXES (default `image`) → raw bytes with that Content-Type, so a vision model can look at it

Anything else is refused rather than dumped as bytes. Exposed as the `read_file` tool. Use /files/view instead when you want the original bytes for a UI preview. Errors: 404 not found, 415 unsupported binary type, 401.

#### Schemas

The model's `read_file` tool. A text file, or a document whose text it extracts (PDF, Office, OpenDocument, …), answers JSON; a binary whose type starts with an OPEN_TERMINAL_BINARY_MIME_PREFIXES entry (`image` by default) answers its raw bytes with that type; any other binary is a 415.

Response `200` (`application/json`) — or, for an image, its bytes:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": true,
  "required": ["path", "total_lines", "content"],
  "properties": {
    "path": {"type": "string"},
    "total_lines": {"type": "integer", "description": "Lines in the whole file"},
    "content": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Lines `start_line`..`end_line` (1-indexed, inclusive)"
    }
  }
}
```

header.description: Open WebUI user id. In multi-user mode this selects which Linux account and /home/<user> the call runs against; the openwebui backend sets it automatically. Omit (or clear the variable) to act as the default `user` account.

query.description: Path to the file.
Best-effort rendered preview (DOCX/PPTX → PDF). Default false.

request.description:
Return the raw bytes of any file with its guessed Content-Type — the UI preview endpoint, with none of /files/read's binary restrictions. With `preview=true`, DOCX and PPTX are rendered to PDF via LibreOffice (present in the default image only); if rendering is unavailable or fails, the original bytes are returned instead, so callers must not assume a PDF came back. Not in the OpenAPI schema. Errors: 404 not found, 401.

#### Schemas

Any file's raw bytes, for the UI (none of `/files/read`'s restrictions). 404 when the file is not there.

Response `200` (`application/octet-stream`) — the bytes, typed by the file's extension (`application/octet-stream` when unknown); with `preview=true` a DOCX / PPTX that LibreOffice renders comes back as `application/pdf`.

header.description: Open WebUI user id. In multi-user mode this selects which Linux account and /home/<user> the call runs against; the openwebui backend sets it automatically. Omit (or clear the variable) to act as the default `user` account.

variable.description: Absolute file path WITHOUT the leading slash, e.g. `home/user/site/index.html`. Postman percent-encodes it as one segment, so for nested paths prefer /files/view?path=… in this collection.

request.description:
Path-addressed alias for /files/view (always `preview=false`). It exists so a previewed HTML page can resolve its own relative asset URLs inside an iframe. The path variable is the ABSOLUTE path with its leading slash dropped — `/home/user/site/index.html` is requested as `/files/serve/home/user/site/index.html`. Not in the OpenAPI schema. Errors: 404 not found, 401.

#### Schemas

`/files/view` addressed by path (`/files/serve/home/user/x.html` serves `/home/user/x.html`), never a preview.

Response `200` (`application/octet-stream`) — the bytes, typed by the file's extension.

item.name: Execute
item.description: Non-interactive command execution. Commands always run in the background behind an id; `wait` only controls how long the server holds the response open. Output is read non-destructively by offset, so several readers can follow the same process. Processes are scoped by the X-User-Id + X-Session-Id pair — GET /execute with different headers shows a different list.

item.name: Terminals (PTY)
item.description:
Interactive pseudo-terminal sessions — the xterm pane in the chat UI — plus the two endpoints a model uses to read from and type into the shell the human already has open.

**The attach endpoint is a WebSocket and cannot be exercised from a collection request.** `GET (ws) /api/terminals/{session_id}` upgrades, then uses FIRST-MESSAGE AUTH: the client's first frame must be the text JSON `{"type": "auth", "token": "<OPEN_TERMINAL_API_KEY>"}` — there is no Authorization header on the upgrade, so the collection-level bearer auth does not apply. After that, keystrokes are sent as BINARY frames and PTY output arrives as binary frames; resize with a text frame `{"type": "resize", "cols": 120, "rows": 40}`. Use Postman's separate WebSocket request type (New → WebSocket), `websocat`, or the Open WebUI UI itself.

Session count is capped globally by OPEN_TERMINAL_MAX_SESSIONS (16); POST /api/terminals returns 429 past it.
